_comment: GENERATED by `python3 -m edge_workbench.prepare`. Do not edit:
re-run it. This is what the build reads instead of the
tutorial, so that a build depends on files in this repository
and not on which branch a sibling checkout happens to be on.
`source.sha` is the commit the tutorial was read at. A gate
compares it against the tutorial's head to tell you when the
tutorial has moved and this needs re-running.
`gaps` lists what the tutorial does not state in a form this
step can read. Those are the model-assisted half's input; an
empty list means the tutorial said everything itself.

example.quote: Take a four-vertex network with source $$s = 0$$, sink $$t = 3$$

meanings.init: Set up the starting state: no flow, no excess, every height 0 except the source, lifted to |V|.
meanings.E01: Saturate every edge leaving the source.
meanings.E02: Record that flow, and the matching negative flow on each reverse edge.
meanings.E03: Excess at each vertex is what arrived minus what left.
meanings.E04: Build the residual graph: source edges are spent, reverse edges back to the source open up.
meanings.E05: Mark the internal vertices, the only ones that may hold excess.
meanings.E06: A vertex is active if it is internal and holding excess.
meanings.E07: Keep the residual edges whose tail is an active vertex.
meanings.E08: An edge runs downhill when d(u) = d(v) + 1.
meanings.E09: Admissible edges: leaving an active vertex, with residual capacity, running downhill.
meanings.E10: Each active vertex picks one admissible edge to push along, any one.
meanings.E11: Send min(excess, residual) along the chosen edge.
meanings.E12: Add the pushed flow forward and subtract it on the reverse edge.
meanings.E13: Total flow arriving at each vertex this round.
meanings.E14: Total flow leaving each vertex this round.
meanings.E15: Excess gains what arrived and loses what left.
meanings.E16: Forward residual shrinks and reverse residual grows, which is what lets flow be undone later.
meanings.E17: Which edges are still admissible after the push.
meanings.E18: Does this vertex still have somewhere to push?
meanings.E19: Recompute the active set against the new excess.
meanings.E20: A vertex still holding excess with nowhere to push must relabel.
meanings.E21: Collect the heights of each relabelling vertex's residual neighbours.
meanings.E22: The lowest neighbour height, per relabelling vertex.
meanings.E23: The new height is one above the lowest neighbour.
meanings.E24: Apply the new heights; every other vertex keeps the one it had.
meanings.stop: No internal vertex holds excess any more, so the flow is maximum.

tensorNotes.F: the flow on each edge at generation $$i$$ (the answer; reverse entries are negative)
tensorNotes.Act: the active internal vertices (those holding excess)

quotes.E01: pushes the full capacity out of every source edge
quotes.E02: adds the reverse residual edges back toward the source
quotes.E04: is the capacity graph with the source row zeroed
quotes.E05: marks the internal vertices (neither source nor sink)
quotes.E06: A vertex is active when it is internal and holds positive excess
quotes.E07: keeps the residual edges leaving an active vertex
quotes.E08: flow may only move strictly downhill by one
quotes.E09: is the set of admissible residual edges out of active vertices
quotes.E11: the smaller of the vertex's excess and the edge's residual
quotes.E12: Flow is then adjusted on the chosen edges and their reverses
quotes.E15: excess is updated by what each vertex received versus sent
quotes.E17: Using the updated residual, recompute the admissible mask
quotes.E18: each vertex still has any admissible edge
quotes.E19: Recompute the active set on the updated excess
quotes.E20: A vertex relabels when it is still active but stuck
quotes.stop:
every unit of preflow has either reached the sink or been
  returned to the source
